X.label: X axis, a diameter
X.description: Position across the turning axis. It is a diameter while diameter programming is on, which is how this profile starts.

C.label: C axis
C.description: Angle of the spindle, used to place holes and flats for driven tools.

Y.label: Y axis
Y.description: Position across the turning axis on machines that have a Y axis.

I.label: Arc centre on X, or a thread lead
I.description: Distance from the start point to the arc centre across the turning axis. In a thread block it is the lead instead, for G34 and G35 the lead at the start of the thread.

J.label: Arc centre on Y, or a thread lead
J.description: Distance from the start point to the arc centre along Y. In a thread block it is the lead instead, for G34 and G35 the lead at the start of the thread.

K.label: Arc centre on Z, or a thread lead
K.description: Distance from the start point to the arc centre along the turning axis. In a thread block it is the lead instead, for G34 and G35 the lead at the start of the thread.

CR.label: Arc radius
CR.description: Radius of an arc, written instead of the centre. A negative radius picks the arc longer than half a circle. It is always written with an equals sign.

AR.label: Opening angle
AR.description: Angle an arc sweeps, written instead of the end point or the centre. It is always written with an equals sign.

LIMS.label: Spindle speed limit
LIMS.description: Highest speed the control may run while the constant cutting speed is on. It is a limit, not a speed: changing it changes the guard the programmer set.

SF.label: Thread start angle
SF.description: Angle at which a thread starts, used for multi-start threads.

D.label: Cutting edge
D.description: Offset set of the active tool. D0 switches the length and radius offsets off.

F.label: Feed, or dwell time
F.description: Feed rate. Its unit follows the feed type in force: a distance per minute with G94, G961 and G971, per spindle revolution with G95, G96, G97 and G973. With G4 it is a dwell in seconds, and with G34 or G35 the change of the thread lead per revolution.

S.label: Spindle speed
S.description: Spindle speed in revolutions per minute, or the cutting speed while G96, G961 or G962 is active. With G4 it is a dwell in spindle revolutions, and with G25 or G26 a speed limit. A number in the address, as in S3=, names the spindle it is for; a plain S is meant for the master spindle, which SETMS can change.

T.label: Tool
T.description: Tool number, or the tool name in quotation marks where the machine manages tools by name. T0 deselects the tool.

N.label: Block number
N.description: Number of the block. It is optional, and the control does not require the numbers to be in order.

L.label: Subprogram call
L.description: Calls the subprogram of that number. The digits are the program's name, leading zeros included, so L12 and L012 call two different programs.

P.label: Repeat count
P.description: How often the subprogram called in the same block runs.

G.label: Preparatory function
G.description: Selects how the control reads the rest of the block: the kind of movement, the plane, the feed mode and the measuring modes.

M.label: Machine function
M.description: Switches a machine function such as the spindle, the coolant or the program end. Numbers above 30 are set up by the machine builder and are not errors.

codes.label: Rapid
codes.description: Moves to the position at rapid speed.

codes.label: Linear feed move
codes.description: Moves to the position on a straight line at the feed in F.

codes.label: Arc, clockwise
codes.description: Cuts an arc clockwise to the end point in the axis words. I, J and K give the centre.

codes.label: Arc, counter-clockwise
codes.description: Cuts an arc counter-clockwise, described the same way as G2.

codes.label: Arc through a point
codes.description: Cuts an arc through an intermediate point given with I1=, J1= and K1=.

codes.label: Arc, tangential
codes.description: Cuts an arc that joins the path before it without a corner. Only the end point is given.

codes.label: Dwell
codes.description: Holds the position for the time in F, in seconds, or for the number of spindle revolutions in S; S2= and the like count the revolutions of another spindle. It stands in a block of its own. That F is not a feed and that S is not a speed, so nothing that scales feeds or speeds may touch them.

codes.label: Tapping with a compensating chuck, one block
codes.description: Taps to the position in the block with the spindle not under position control; the chuck takes up the difference. F has to be the spindle speed times the thread pitch, so the two may only be changed together. The move type in force before it applies again in the next block.

codes.label: Exact stop, this block only
codes.description: Brings the axes to a stop inside the position window at the end of this block, without changing the path mode that follows.

codes.label: Exact stop mode
codes.description: Stops at the end of every block until another path mode replaces it, so each corner is cut sharp.

codes.label: Continuous path mode
codes.description: Keeps the axes moving from one block into the next instead of stopping at every block end; the control slows down at a corner as far as it has to.

codes.label: Continuous path, rounded by distance
codes.description: Rounds a corner within the distance given by ADIS.

codes.label: Continuous path, rounded by axis tolerance
codes.description: Rounds a corner within the tolerance each axis is allowed. Programs written by CAM often carry it.

codes.label: Continuous path, rounded on tangential corners too
Working plane ZX
codes.description: The plane a turning program works in.

codes.label: Thread cutting
codes.description: Cuts a thread with a constant lead, given in I, J or K. The lead is not a feed and may never be scaled like one.

codes.label: Rigid tapping, into the hole
codes.description: Drives the tap with the spindle under position control; the lead is in I, J or K and is not a feed. S is read in revolutions per minute here, whatever the feed type says.

codes.label: Rigid tapping, back out
codes.description: The retract of a rigid tapping pass, with the same lead as the block that cut it.

codes.label: Thread cutting, lead growing
codes.description: Cuts a thread whose lead grows along the thread: I, J or K give the lead at the start, and F the change of the lead per revolution. Neither is a feed, and nothing may scale them.

codes.label: Thread cutting, lead shrinking
codes.description: Cuts a thread whose lead shrinks along the thread: I, J or K give the lead at the start, and F the change of the lead per revolution. Neither is a feed, and nothing may scale them.

codes.label: Thread along an arc, clockwise
codes.description: Cuts a thread whose path is a clockwise arc instead of a straight line. The lead is in I, J or K as with G33, so the arc centre is written as IR=, JR= and KR=.

codes.label: Thread along an arc, counter-clockwise
codes.description: Cuts a thread whose path is a counter-clockwise arc instead of a straight line. The lead is in I, J or K as with G33, so the arc centre is written as IR=, JR= and KR=.

codes.label: Radius compensation, tool left
codes.description: Offsets the path by the radius of the edge that D selects, seen along the direction of travel.

codes.label: Suppress the offsets for this block
codes.description: Runs this block without the work offsets.

codes.label: Suppress the offsets for this block, more of them than G53
codes.description: Leaves out more of the offsets than G53 does, for this block only. Programs use it to move to a machine position, as before a tool change.

codes.label: Settable work offset off
codes.description: Cancels the settable work offset. Programs often write it in the header.

codes.label: Inch for the geometry
codes.description: Reads the positions as inches. It is a unit switch on this control and not a finishing cycle.

codes.label: Millimetres for the geometry
codes.description: Reads the positions as millimetres. It is a unit switch on this control and not a roughing cycle.

codes.label: Inch for the geometry and the feed
Millimetres for the geometry and the feed
Absolute positions
codes.description: Reads every position as a distance from the zero point.

codes.label: Incremental positions
codes.description: Reads every position as a distance from the point before.

codes.label: Inverse-time feed
codes.description: F is the reciprocal of the time the block takes, not a distance. It also ends a constant cutting speed, so S is in revolutions per minute.

codes.label: Feed per minute
codes.description: F is a distance per minute from here on, and S a speed in revolutions per minute: it also ends a constant cutting speed.

codes.label: Feed per revolution
codes.description: F is a distance per spindle revolution from here on, which is how turning programs cut, and S a speed in revolutions per minute: it also ends a constant cutting speed.

codes.label: Constant cutting speed, feed per revolution
codes.description: S is a cutting speed from here on, and the control changes the spindle speed with the diameter. It also makes F a distance per revolution. A speed limit belongs with it, written as LIMS=.

codes.label: Fixed spindle speed, feed per revolution
codes.description: S is a speed in revolutions per minute again, and F a distance per revolution. Without a new S the spindle keeps the speed it was turning at.

codes.label: Constant cutting speed, feed per minute
codes.description: As G96, but F is a distance per minute.

codes.label: Constant cutting speed, feed type kept
codes.description: As G96, but F keeps the unit it had: per minute or per revolution.

codes.label: Fixed spindle speed, feed per minute
codes.description: As G97, but F is a distance per minute. A LIMS= limit does not act under it.

codes.label: Fixed spindle speed, feed type kept
codes.description: As G97, but F keeps the unit it had: per minute or per revolution.

codes.label: Fixed spindle speed without a speed limit
codes.description: As G97, but no LIMS= limit is switched on with it.

codes.label: Feed per minute, spindle speed frozen
codes.description: F is a distance per minute, and the spindle keeps the speed it is turning at, whether a cutting speed or an S set it.

codes.label: Feed per revolution, spindle speed frozen
codes.description: F is a distance per revolution, and the spindle keeps the speed it is turning at, whether a cutting speed or an S set it.

codes.label: Lower limit: spindle speed with S, working area with axis words
codes.description: With S the lowest speed the master spindle may run at, and S2=, S3= set it for the spindle of that number; with axis words the lower end of the working area. Either way it is a limit, not a speed or a position to move to. The control stores it in its settings, so it can still be in force after the program ends.

codes.label: Upper limit: spindle speed with S, working area with axis words
codes.description: With S the highest speed the master spindle may run at, and S2=, S3= set it for the spindle of that number; with axis words the upper end of the working area. Either way it is a limit, not a speed or a position to move to. The control stores it in its settings, so it can still be in force after the program ends.

codes.label: Diameter programming on
codes.description: Reads the cross axis as a diameter from here on. gEdit also assumes it at the start of a program, unless the machine configuration says the control starts without it.

codes.label: Diameter programming off
codes.description: Reads the cross axis as a radius from here on.

codes.label: Diameter for absolute values only
codes.description: Reads absolute positions on the cross axis as diameters and incremental ones as radii.

codes.label: Drilling or centring cycle
codes.description: Drills to depth in one pass and retracts. The plane, the depth and the safety distance come in the order below.

codes.description: Drills to depth, waits there and retracts, which is what a counterbore needs.

codes.description: Drills in pecks, so the chips break or leave the hole. VARI decides between breaking the chip and pulling the drill out.

codes.description: Cuts the thread with the spindle under position control, so no compensating chuck is needed. The lead (MPIT or PIT) and the tapping speed (SST) are its own arguments: it does not take its lead from the feed in force.

codes.description: Feeds in and feeds back out, so the bore keeps its finish. The two feeds are given separately.

codes.description: Stops the spindle at an angle at depth, lifts the tool off the wall and pulls it out at rapid.

codes.description: Stops the spindle and the program at depth; the operator retracts the tool.

codes.description: Waits at depth, then stops the spindle and the program there.

codes.label: Grooving cycle
codes.description: Cuts a groove on the outside, the inside or the face. The name is recognised; the parameters are not described yet.

codes.label: Stock removal cycle
codes.description: Roughs and finishes along a contour that a subprogram describes. Its three feeds, for roughing, for plunging into undercuts and for finishing, are arguments.

codes.label: Thread chain cycle
codes.description: Cuts several thread sections one after the other. The lead is one of its arguments. The parameters are not described yet.

codes.label: Contour call
codes.description: Names the contour the turning cycle after it works on. It cuts nothing itself.

codes.label: Program stop
codes.description: Stops the program until the operator starts it again.

codes.label: Optional stop
codes.description: Stops the program when the operator has switched optional stop on.

codes.label: End of subprogram
codes.description: Ends a subprogram and goes on after the block that called it.

codes.label: Spindle on, clockwise
codes.description: Starts the master spindle clockwise. M3=3 does the same for spindle 3.

codes.label: Spindle on, counter-clockwise
codes.description: Starts the master spindle counter-clockwise. M3=4 does the same for spindle 3.

codes.label: Spindle stop
codes.description: Stops the master spindle. M3=5 stops spindle 3.

codes.label: Tool change
codes.description: Carries out the change on a machine with a magazine. Whether a turret changes on the T word alone or needs this code is set up on the machine.

codes.label: Spindle orientation
codes.description: Turns the spindle to the angle kept in the control's setting data and holds it there until the next M3, M4 or M5. M2=19 does the same for spindle 2.

codes.label: Choose the master spindle
codes.description: SETMS(3) makes spindle 3 the master spindle, so the S, M3, M4 and M5 that follow without a spindle number are meant for it. SETMS on its own goes back to the master spindle the machine is set up with. It stands in a block of its own.

codes.label: Operator message
codes.description: Shows the text in the brackets on the control. MSG() with nothing inside clears it.

codes.label: Modal cycle call
codes.description: Makes the cycle or subprogram written after it run after every following block that moves, until MCALL stands on its own.

codes.label: Stop the look-ahead
codes.description: Makes the control finish the blocks it has already read before it goes on.

codes.label: Suppress the offsets for this block, all of them
codes.description: The widest of G53, G153 and SUPA: this block runs in machine coordinates.

codes.label: Face transformation on
codes.description: Turns on the transformation that lets a driven tool work on the face with X and Y.

codes.label: Transformation off
codes.description: Ends the transformation that is running.

codes.label: Programmable offset
codes.description: Shifts the zero point by the values in the block. Written on its own it clears the programmable frame.

codes.label: Compressor on
codes.description: Joins short straight blocks into a smoother path.

codes.label: Interpolate the orientation axis by axis
Interpolate the orientation as a vector
This value is absolute
codes.description: Reads the one value in brackets as an absolute position, whatever the distance mode says.

codes.label: Jump forward
codes.description: Continues at the label, searching towards the end of the program.

codes.label: Jump backward
codes.description: Continues at the label, searching towards the start of the program.

codes.label: Jump
codes.description: Continues at the label or the block number, searching forwards first and then backwards.

codes.label: Jump without an alarm
codes.description: Like GOTO, but the control does not stop when the target is missing.

codes.label: Conditional
codes.description: Runs what follows when the condition holds.

codes.label: Upper bound of a counting loop
Repeat loop, or a section between two labels
Branch of CASE for every other value
Return from a subprogram
codes.description: Returns from a subprogram to the block after the call, as M17 does. It stands in a block of its own.

codes.label: Subprogram head
codes.description: Names a subprogram and the values it takes. It is the first statement of the program.

codes.label: Declare a subprogram
codes.description: Tells the calling program the name and the values of a subprogram that is not in the cycle folders.

codes.label: Declare a variable
codes.description: Declares a variable of the program. The declarations stand at the top of the program, one DEF per block.

codes.label: Indirect call
codes.description: Calls a program whose name stands in quotation marks or in a variable.

codes.label: Call with a path
codes.description: Calls a subprogram by its full path, with arguments: PCALL/path/NAME(…).

codes.label: Call from external storage
codes.description: Runs a program from a drive outside the control's program memory, such as a local, network or USB drive, named in quotation marks in brackets: EXTCALL("…").

codes.label: Section of a program
codes.description: CALL … BLOCK start TO end runs the part of a program between two labels.
